group_assessment.waived: The two publication counts cannot be measured: the PubMed connector is unauthorized in this session, and an estimate in an integer slot is indistinguishable from a measurement. What the paper itself establishes is recorded here so the waiver loses nothing. research_type is descriptive_clinical: a 13-patient, 12-family, five-centre international cohort with source EEG and MRI reviewed centrally, ACMG re-classification of all literature variants, and Kaplan-Meier survival analysis; RNA/RT-PCR work was performed but only to resolve the pathogenicity of two CNVs, so it is confirmatory rather than mechanistic. is_primary_group_for_disease is false in the strict sense — this is a leading epilepsy-genetics network (Scheffer, Bahlo, Hildebrand, Mefford, Specchio), not a WWOX laboratory — but it is as close to a primary group as WWOX-DEE currently has, because the disease's evidence base is clinical cohorts and this is the largest. Weighting: the observations carry high weight (centralised re-review of primary EEG and MRI, not abstracted from reports; variants re-classified rather than accepted). The survival analysis is the weakest link and the paper does not flag it: n = 75 split three ways, and the p-value is a three-group log-rank presented alongside a pairwise conclusion. NOTE: the waiver is per-section but the impediment is per-field — declining two unmeasurable integers also discards three fields determined from the Methods.

entries.proposition: The paper explicitly finds NO evidence for an intermediate genotype class: carrying one versus two missense variants made no difference, and missense-carrying WWOX-DEE patients were as severe as null/null patients.
entries.snippet: We found no difference between individuals with one or two missense variants and therefore no evidence to support an "intermediate" phenotype, as our WWOX-DEE patients were as severe as those with two loss-of-function null alleles.

entries.proposition: Survival separates null/null from anything carrying a missense allele; the statistic is a three-group log-rank.
entries.snippet: Using the Kaplan-Meier method to analyze time to death, we found that survival was much poorer for the double null group compared with the patients who had at least one missense pathogenic variant (p-value = .0085, log-rank test).

entries.proposition: The 5-year survival figures cited downstream as a genotype effect.
entries.snippet: Probability of survival to the age of 5 years for the double null group was <50%; by comparison, it was >75% for the other two, presumably less severe, genetic groups

entries.proposition: Genotype class does not predict age at seizure onset — a negative result on a different axis from survival.
entries.snippet: we found no difference in time to seizure onset between the three genetic groups (p-value = .65, log-rank test)

entries.proposition: No region of WWOX is specific to the DEE phenotype, and the two SCAR12 missense variants sit close to DEE variants rather than in a separate domain.
entries.snippet: no region of the gene emerged as specific for being associated with WWOX-DEE. Furthermore, the two missense variants associated with the rarer, milder SCAR12 phenotype are situated in close proximity to WWOX-DEE variants: p.Gly372Arg in exon 9 and p.Pro47Thr in exon 2.

entries.proposition: The same codon produces both disease poles depending on the substitution: Pro47Thr in SCAR12, Pro47Arg in WWOX-DEE.
entries.snippet: p.Pro47 has been associated with two pathogenic variants; the more conservative change to threonine was found in SCAR12 compared with the arginine substitution found in WWOX-DEE

entries.proposition: Lennox-Gastaut syndrome was excluded in this cohort on the EEG hallmark, and the authors note the hallmark was never reported in the cases previously labelled LGS.
entries.snippet: Although our patients had multiple seizure types, they did not show the mandatory EEG hallmark of LGS of <2.5 Hz slow spike-wave, excluding this syndromic diagnosis. It is notable that this EEG feature was not reported for patients previously classified as LGS.

entries.proposition: Mortality is 35% across the combined series, driven by respiratory complications.
entries.snippet: WWOX-DEE has a high mortality rate of 35%, with 23 of 62 individuals deceased in the literature and 3 of 13 patients here.

entries.proposition: A distinctive MRI pattern is present and is detectable within days of birth, not only after seizure burden accumulates.
entries.snippet: We identified a WWOX-DEE pattern of severe frontotemporal atrophy, hippocampal atrophy, very thin corpus callosum, optic atrophy, and white matter signal abnormalities. These findings were evident from as early as 15 days of life, with repeat MRI revealing increased cerebral atrophy over time.

entries.proposition: Optic atrophy was universal and age-independent in the cohort.
entries.snippet: All cases demonstrated severe optic atrophy, irrespective of age, and some patients showed brainstem changes, which were mainly dorsal

entries.proposition: No patient developed a tumour despite WWOX being an established tumour suppressor; the authors attribute this to early mortality rather than to absence of risk.
entries.snippet: there are no reports of WWOX-DEE or SCAR12 patients with tumors; however, this could simply be due to the high early mortality rate of WWOX-DEE

entries.proposition: Severe hypomyelination is reproduced across rodent models and in human WWOX-deficient brain organoids, giving a human in-vitro system for the myelin axis.
entries.snippet: the brains of Wwox-mutant rodents demonstrate severe hypomyelination, a finding more recently observed in human WWOX-deficient brain organoids.

entries.proposition: WWOX is proposed as a candidate gene for genetically undiagnosed PEHO and PEHO-like syndrome.
entries.snippet: this makes WWOX a plausible candidate gene for patients with PEHO or PEHO-like syndrome that remain without a genetic diagnosis.

entries.proposition: One third of cases required chromosomal microarray alongside sequencing; sequencing alone would have missed them.
entries.snippet: Without this dual approach, one third of our WWOX-DEE cases would have been missed.

entries.proposition: No patient in the cohort achieved independent walking, irrespective of genotype class.
entries.snippet: None achieved independent walking, and only two had a single word, whereas 11 were nonverbal.

entries.proposition: The oldest living WWOX-DEE patient reported at the time of publication was 23 years 11 months.
entries.snippet: We report the oldest living patient, aged 23 years 11 months.

entries.proposition: In the longest-followed patient the EEG evolved over two decades from multifocal epileptiform activity to a diffuse low-voltage background with no epileptiform abnormalities at all.
entries.snippet: Patient 2, with the longest follow-up (21 years), showed progression to a diffuse low-voltage background without epileptiform abnormalities

entries.proposition: That longest-followed, oldest-living patient is homozygous for the missense p.Gln230Pro, i.e. missense/missense.
entries.snippet: c.689A > C, p.Gln230Pro (homozygous)
entries.anchor: Table 1, Patient 2 — read together with the same column's 'Age, sex: 23 y 11 m, M' and 'Genetic combination: Missense/missense'

entries.proposition: Read from the figure image rather than its caption: survival curves order null/missense above missense/missense above null/null, with the top two heavily overlapping in their 95% bands — consistent with the text's own statement that one versus two missense variants made no difference, and inconsistent with reading p = .0085 as a graded three-step ranking.
entries.snippet: Survival analysis for 75 individuals with WWOX developmental and epileptic encephalopathy stratified by genetic variant group. (A) Time to death. (B) Time to seizure onset.
entries.anchor: Figure 4, image inspected — panel A curves, censoring ticks and shaded 95% CI bands; panel B carries p = .65 on its face

entries.proposition: Read from the figure image: the two SCAR12-associated missense variants are marked at opposite ends of the protein, exon 2 and exon 9, interleaved with DEE variants rather than clustered.
entries.snippet: Location and type of pathogenic WWOX variants in our cohort (top) of 13 patients and those from the literature (bottom).
